success_semantics: Verified means the named Go verifier established the deterministic postcondition and terminal evidence became durable
refusal_semantics: Rejected input does not execute and unsupported input bytes are not retained
failure_semantics: Execution, protocol or verification failure cannot become verified
cancellation_semantics: Cancellation attempts bounded termination and reports cleanup complete only after observing the complete owned process tree empty
indeterminate_semantics: Missing, contradictory or non-durable required evidence is never treated as allowed or verified
recovery_semantics: Recovery removes uncommitted staging, never reruns the worker and publishes committed interrupted attempts as indeterminate
compatibility_or_reset_policy: No pre-release persistence compatibility is promised before operational retention begins
